audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for John the Baptist, metanoeite, reign/realm of the heavens, wilderness Isaiah voice, Pharisees/Sadducees, fruit language, axe/root, Spirit and fire baptism, winnowing imagery, and Jesus' baptism/theophany.

verses.restored: In those days John the Baptist came proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea,

familiar.text: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,

modern.text: In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea

original.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις παραγίνεται Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς κηρύσσων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τῆς Ἰουδαίας

verses.restored: saying, Turn and realign your mind/heart, for the reign of the heavens has drawn near.

familiar.text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.

modern.text: and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ λέγων· Μετανοεῖτε, ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν.

verses.restored: For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet: A voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.

familiar.text: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

modern.text: This is he who was spoken of through the prophet Isaiah: “A voice of one calling in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.’”

original.text: οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ ῥηθεὶς ⸀διὰ Ἠσαΐου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: John himself had clothing from camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.

familiar.text: And the same John had his raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.

modern.text: John wore a garment of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

original.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰωάννης εἶχεν τὸ ἔνδυμα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τριχῶν καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, ἡ δὲ τροφὴ ⸂ἦν αὐτοῦ⸃ ἀκρίδες καὶ μέλι ἄγριον.

verses.restored: Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him.

familiar.text: Then went out to him Jerusalem, and all Judaea, and all the region round about Jordan,

modern.text: People went out to him from Jerusalem and all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan.

original.text: τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου,

verses.restored: They were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: And were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.

modern.text: Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.

original.text: καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ⸀ποταμῷ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: Seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to the baptism, he said to them, Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

familiar.text: But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?

modern.text: But when John saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his place of baptism, he said to them, “You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?

original.text: Ἰδὼν δὲ πολλοὺς τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ Σαδδουκαίων ἐρχομένους ἐπὶ τὸ βάπτισμα ⸀αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;

verses.restored: Therefore produce fruit worthy of turning/realignment.

familiar.text: Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance:

modern.text: Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance.

original.text: ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας

verses.restored: Do not suppose you can say among yourselves, We have Abraham as father; for I say to you that the Divine is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.

familiar.text: And think not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, that God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.

modern.text: And do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that out of these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.

original.text: καὶ μὴ δόξητε λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Πατέρα ἔχομεν τὸν Ἀβραάμ, λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι δύναται ὁ θεὸς ἐκ τῶν λίθων τούτων ἐγεῖραι τέκνα τῷ Ἀβραάμ.

verses.restored: Already the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing beautiful/good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.

familiar.text: And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.

modern.text: The axe lies ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

original.text: ἤδη ⸀δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται.

verses.restored: I baptize you in water for turning/realignment, but the one coming after me is stronger than I; I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you in holy Spirit and fire.

familiar.text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire:

modern.text: I baptize you with water for repentance, but after me will come One more powerful than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

original.text: Ἐγὼ μὲν ⸂ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω⸃ ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ ⸂καὶ πυρί⸃·

verses.restored: His winnowing fork is in his hand. He will thoroughly clear his threshing floor, gather his wheat into the storehouse, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.

familiar.text: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.

modern.text: His winnowing fork is in His hand to clear His threshing floor and to gather His wheat into the barn; but He will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.” The Baptism of Jesus (Mark 1:9–11; Luke 3:21–22; John 1:29–34)

original.text: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ⸀ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ.

verses.restored: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.

familiar.text: Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.

modern.text: At that time Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.

original.text: Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: But John tried to prevent him, saying, I have need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?

familiar.text: But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?

modern.text: But John tried to prevent Him, saying, “I need to be baptized by You, and do You come to me?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀Ἰωάννης διεκώλυεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, Allow it now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness/justice. Then he allowed him.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.

modern.text: “Let it be so now,” Jesus replied. “It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way.” Then John permitted Him.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν ⸂πρὸς αὐτόν⸃· Ἄφες ἄρτι, οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην. τότε ἀφίησιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: After being baptized, Jesus immediately came up from the water; and look, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of the Divine descending like a dove and coming upon him.

familiar.text: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:

modern.text: As soon as Jesus was baptized, He went up out of the water. Suddenly the heavens were opened, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and resting on Him.

original.text: ⸂βαπτισθεὶς δὲ⸃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ⸂εὐθὺς ἀνέβη⸃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕδατος· καὶ ἰδοὺ ⸀ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ οὐρανοί, καὶ εἶδεν ⸀πνεῦμα θεοῦ καταβαῖνον ὡσεὶ ⸀περιστερὰν ἐρχόμενον ἐπʼ αὐτόν·

verses.restored: And look, a voice from the heavens said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I delight.

familiar.text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

modern.text: And a voice from heaven said, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!”

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῶν οὐρανῶν λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα.
